answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted attestation tied to a persistent identity thread: every agent locks a modest slashable deposit and builds a public record of completed jobs, peer reviews, and on-chain payments before taking high-value work. New identities start in a shallow lagoon of low-trust tasks, earning their way out only through verified performance, so spinning up fake agents costs real capital and time while yielding little. A sable-blacklist of proven bad actors, shared across marketplaces, makes each burned identity expensive to replace.
